result.title: ObjectTwin: Measuring the Asset Correspondence Gap for Capture-Anchored Digital Twins
result.summary: Object-wise reconstruction increasingly inserts generated meshes into captured scenes as editable proxies for observed objects. This use creates a requirement absent from isolated-asset scores and pose estimates: at the captured metric state, the proxy should reproduce calibrated observations of the same instance. We present ObjectTwin, a scan-grounded measurement protocol that freezes the instance, cameras, scan-projected support and recorded depth, metric anchor, and evaluation denominator, then replaces only the object representation. The resulting asset correspondence gap measures lost observation agreement relative to scan-derived visible geometry without treating the scan as complete physical ground truth. Across two indoor RGB-D capture domains and two generation backends, visible, anchored generated assets lose 0.302-0.497 MaskIoU under this replacement. Every tested scene-level estimate is positive, while same-input generator preference reverses across capture domains. Coverage and overlap-depth analyses locate disagreement in both visible support and surface placement; the evaluated conservative pose refinement does not systematically recover it. These results establish capture correspondence as a separately measurable interface between generated-asset quality and stronger physical or task-level evaluation.

AI.brief_summary: 提出 ObjectTwin 这一以扫描为锚的测量协议：冻结实例、相机、扫描投影支撑区、深度与评价分母，只替换物体表示，从而量化生成资产相对观测几何的「资产对应性缺口」。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「冻结其余条件、仅替换内部表示、度量观测一致性损失」的干预式协议思路，可能可供核查能否用于评价 LVR 中 latent 状态是否保留视觉证据；但该文本身针对三维资产生成，与推理机制无直接联系。
